price_why: It hands me a first carousel I can shoot at my kitchen table tonight, with the cover, slide order and follow-ups already worked out. But much of the text is research apparatus and odd jargon I'd have to wade through.
one_line: A heavily researched brief whose main recommendation is a nine-slide carousel of a Partridge and Orange laid out as an exploded diagram, with three ranked follow-up posts.
strongest: The exploded-materials cover is very specific and easy to make: parts in one row, in order of use, unlabelled. Paired with one action per slide, each opening on the last slide's result, it suits beginners learning to tie.
weakest: The hook is left as an abstract recipe ('a bare count and a flat claim') instead of an actual line. Useful ideas are also buried under dense research notes, blocked-page logs and unexplained jargon like 'register' and 'carry'.
